_comment: ADR-0041 RI-3. The hard-identifier wall exists in TWO languages — Python
(`app/pseudonymize.contains_hard_identifier`, gate 6 on the ai-service) and TypeScript
anything is persisted). Two implementations of one privacy rule is a drift hazard, and
the usual fix — read the other language's source and compare — does not work here: the
credential-id patterns use inline case-insensitive groups and lookaheads whose syntax
differs between the two engines, so the regexes cannot be identical even when the
So this file pins the behaviour instead, and both suites read it. A case added here
fails whichever side has not implemented it. `expected` is the class name, or null when
the value must be PERMITTED — and the permitted half is the half that matters most:
ADR-0041 D5 authorises employer names, and certifying résumé values with the full
pseudonymization gateway would reject nearly every honest value while the ruling says to
keep them. A wall that refuses the honest cases is a wall someone deletes.
THE SEPARATOR CASES EXIST BECAUSE THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS FILE PROVED NOTHING. Every
case used a space, while the two implementations' separator sets diverged in BOTH
directions — the TS side was missing `;`, `|` and the whole Unicode set, and had added
`/` and backslash the far side does not have. The cross-language pin verified none of
the actual divergence. Found by the RI-3 security review.

cases._group: separators the two implementations disagreed about

cases._note: A KNOWN, PINNED GAP ON BOTH SIDES, not a difference of opinion. `/` is absent from the gateway's separator set (an R30 residual), and widening the SHARED pattern would change what the interview masks — not something a résumé change gets to do. Recorded here so the gap is a fact somebody decided rather than one nobody noticed.

ONLY THE INVISIBLE-STRIP CATCHES THIS. `PAN_RE` has no separator tolerance, so a zero-width space inside a PAN defeats it on both sides unless the character is removed before matching. Without this case the strip was redundant on every other case in the file and a mutation removing it passed.

cases._group: the 14+ band nothing covered until the RI-3 review
must be PERMITTED — ADR-0041 D5 and ordinary trade vocabulary

cases._note: The digit lookahead in the cued pattern is what keeps these three permitted. Without it, `\baccount\b` or `\bvoter\b` plus the next word refuses a job title a real worker holds.
